observations: Photo 0 shows a dry pressing iron (no visible water tank) with a damaged/dirty-looking power cord and plug area.
Iron soleplate area is visible but not clearly clean; no clear brand/model label is readable.
No photo shows it switched on, heating, or any temperature control working.

claims.claim: A used dry pressing iron that is still working is available for sale.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 does not show the iron plugged in or heating; cord/plug area looks worn/damaged.

risks.risk: Not actually working (no heating test shown).
risks.proof: A short video of the iron plugged in with temperature dial set, showing it heats (e.g., indicator/heat-up) and stays on.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not working / needs repair.

risks.risk: Electrical safety risk from worn/damaged cord/plug (visible wear near the plug and along the cable).
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the plug pins and cable entry + a quick continuity test/inspection screenshot from a technician (or seller shows it sparks/does not).
risks.if_unproven: Price as unsafe to use until cord is replaced.

risks.risk: Soleplate condition may be poor (staining/scuffs) affecting ironing quality.
risks.proof: Photo of the soleplate close-up in good light + a test ironing a small fabric piece.

risks.risk: No brand/model identification; wattage and build quality unknown.
risks.proof: Photo of the rating label (bottom/back) showing brand and wattage.
risks.if_unproven: Price at the lowest end for generic dry irons.

proof_requests: Send a video of the iron plugged in and heating (show it working for at least 2–3 minutes).
Send clear close-up photos of the plug and the entire cord (especially where it looks worn).
Send a photo of the rating/brand label (bottom/back) showing wattage.
Show a quick test ironing on a small cloth.
response.reason: It is clearly a dry pressing iron, but the only photo shows worn/damaged cord/plug and provides no proof it heats; so it must be priced at the worst case (not working/needs repair) using the cheapest matching comparables.
